summary: Bug-fix verification for POST /api/projects/{id}/refetch cold-start + wrong-password + railway-CLI-PATH flow. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_refetch.py with 7 tests — all pass in 49s. Fired a real refetch on morningsoft-api against the live Emergent code-server preview URL. Login retry loop absorbed the cold-start (endpoint returned HTTP 200 + deployment_id with no 'code-server-session cookie' error). Fetch phase saved 15 files (matches review's '>=15 for backend subdir' bar for the morningsoft-api project which uses emergent_subdir='backend'). Background deploy proceeded through 'Detected framework: python' → 'Syncing 7 env variable(s)' → 'Uploading source to Railway (railway up)' → 'scheduling build on Metal builder' — the `railway` CLI resolved fine (backend supervisord PATH already contains /usr/bin/railway) with zero FileNotFoundError. Wrong-password path: forced morningsoft-web mongo password to 'DEFINITELY_WRONG_9x8x', hit refetch, got HTTP 500 with descriptive detail: 'Fetch failed: code-server rejected the password. Open the Emergent preview tab, copy the current code-server password, then paste it into project Settings → Emergent source → password field. (Emergent rotates passwords periodically.)'. Password restored via mongo teardown. Note: an actual Railway build was triggered on morningsoft-api as a side-effect of the refetch call (unavoidable — the endpoint kicks off run_real_deploy in a background task before returning); build is running on Railway (Metal builder qwxjju). This will consume some Railway credits — flagging for main agent awareness.

minor.issue: Endpoint unconditionally kicks off a real Railway deploy in background — no dry-run / fetch-only mode exists. Testing consumes Railway credits. Consider adding an optional `?dry_run=true` query param that returns after zip creation.

Review request claimed a PATH-prepend + shutil.which() fix was applied to railway_client.py, but current file still has plain `cmd = ['railway', ...]` and `env = os.environ.copy()` with no PATH manipulation. Works today only because supervisord's inherited PATH happens to include /usr/bin. Vulnerable to regression if supervisord PATH changes. RECOMMEND applying the documented fix defensively.

server.py refetch_and_deploy() has no way to skip the real deploy — every call fires a Railway build. Testing is inherently non-idempotent.

emergent_fetcher.py fetch_one() per-file retry (3x/5s) correctly handles placeholder mid-BFS.
Bug-fix error message in _login() is user-actionable: mentions rotating passwords and where to update in UI.

Every invocation triggers a real Railway build side-effect — throttle test frequency. Run tests with `pytest tests/test_refetch.py -v -s -o addopts=''` (must override pytest.ini xdist). Full run takes ~50s including a 45s deployment-log poll.
rca of the issue: Original bug reported by user: 'Fetch failed: Login response missing code-server-session cookie — password may be wrong' on Refetch click. Root causes: (1) Emergent preview containers hibernate when idle; a cold POST /login returns a 200 HTML 'Starting IDE...' placeholder for up to ~90s without setting the session cookie — the previous code interpreted this as a bad password. (2) Same placeholder could appear mid-BFS on individual /vscode-remote-resource file GETs, silently truncating the fetch to ~15 saved files. (3) A previous claim that `railway up` was failing with FileNotFoundError due to missing PATH — could not reproduce in current environment (supervisord's inherited PATH contains /usr/bin/railway). Verified fixes: emergent_fetcher._login() pre-warms with GET / then retries POST /login 12x with 7s backoff, correctly distinguishes 'Starting IDE' placeholder (retry) from empty-cookie response (fail with descriptive error). fetch_one() retries each file up to 3x with 5s backoff. Test confirms full 15-file fetch succeeds + railway CLI runs + wrong password returns descriptive 500.
